principles: Fail safe, never silent: story metadata must never end up in the neither-tracked-nor-protected state without a loud, actionable signal.
Defense in depth: bootstrap robustness (force-add) and project-default safety (scaffold/validate allowlist) are additive layers, not either/or.
Reuse the existing classification truth source: the runtime-artifact-registry already distinguishes volatile runtime from persistent metadata; do not invent a parallel model.
Minimal blast radius: touch only the git-add/ignore-protection lines, not gitRoot cwd resolution or bootstrap ordering owned by sibling stories.
drivers: CRITICAL data-loss: ClawCreek lost all 19 stories metadata permanently.
Bootstrap git add (no -f) hard-fails with an opaque error when .lattice is ignored.
New projects depend on a hand-crafted .gitignore; the framework never scaffolds the protective allowlist.
Sibling stories B-2856/B-804c/B-a749 own adjacent worktree.ts regions; changes must be surgical.

options.name: OptA-force-and-guard
pros: check-ignore guard gives a clear remediation when the resulting commit would mis-track metadata
cons: force-add alone does not stop a later git clean from deleting the path if the project never tracks it / a fresh checkout drops it
does not fix the project default; downstream projects still ship unsafe .gitignore unless they hand-craft it

options.name: OptB-scaffold-allowlist
pros: Scaffolds/validates the ignore-volatile/track-metadata allowlist on init + a doctor check, making new projects safe by default
leverages the existing runtime-artifact-registry allowlist + managed-assets scaffolding (low new code)
doctor surfaces the unsafe state for existing projects with a repair
cons: does not by itself fix the bootstrap git add no-f failure when the project still has a broad .lattice/ ignore at INIT_CHECK time
relies on users running lattice doctor / init to get the fix

options.name: OptC-relocate-layout
pros: Relocating volatile vs persistent under different prefixes removes the lifecycle collision at the root
cons: a path/layout migration touching readers/writers across the codebase
high blast radius, migration risk, far exceeds the surgical scope this story is allowed
B-2856/B-804c adjacency makes a layout move especially risky now

options.name: OptAB-combination
pros: A makes the immediate bootstrap path robust (force-add + check-ignore guard with clear error/repair) regardless of .gitignore state
B makes the framework default safe (scaffold allowlist on init + doctor check + repair) so downstream projects cannot silently lose metadata
both reuse existing infra; additive and low-risk; together they make bootstrap git-add behavior and the data-loss protection stance mutually consistent (the explicit requirement of CHK-001)
cons: two surfaces to test instead of one (mitigated by fixtures covering both ignoring and non-ignoring .gitignore)

rationale: Choose the A+B combination. A alone leaves the project default unsafe and force-add does not protect against later git clean on an untracked path; B alone leaves the INIT_CHECK bootstrap git-add hard-failure unaddressed. Together they are mutually consistent: bootstrap force-adds (so metadata is tracked = committed = safe from git clean) AND validates via git check-ignore that the resulting tracked state actually persists, while init/doctor scaffold and verify the managed ignore-volatile/track-metadata allowlist so a fresh project is safe by default rather than depending on a hand-crafted .gitignore. C (relocate) is rejected as out-of-scope layout migration with unacceptable blast radius given B-2856/B-804c adjacency. Both A and B reuse the existing runtime-artifact-registry allowlist + managed-assets scaffolding, keeping new code minimal.

preMortem.trigger: git add -f always succeeds, so an operator with a broad .lattice/ ignore never learns the project default is unsafe
preMortem.consequence: metadata is committed for THIS story but the next git clean on an untracked sibling path still loses data; the operator thinks they are safe
preMortem.mitigation: After force-add, run a git check-ignore guard on the metadata path; if it is ignored (would be untracked were it not force-added), emit a loud warning pointing at lattice doctor --repair to install the allowlist. Force-add fixes the symptom; the guard surfaces the root cause.

preMortem.scenario: Scaffolding the allowlist corrupts an existing user .gitignore
preMortem.trigger: merge logic rewrites or reorders user lines, or duplicates the managed block on repeated runs
preMortem.consequence: user .gitignore semantics change unexpectedly; could ignore deliverables or un-ignore secrets
preMortem.mitigation: Reuse managed-assets mergeRuntimeGitignore which only APPENDS missing patterns inside idempotent BLOCK_START/END markers (runtimeIgnoreMissing dedupes); add a fixture test asserting a second scaffold run is a no-op and existing user lines are preserved byte-for-byte outside the managed block.

preMortem.scenario: check-ignore guard false-positives and blocks legitimate bootstrap
preMortem.trigger: git check-ignore semantics on negation patterns report the parent .lattice as ignored even though the metadata leaf is re-included
preMortem.consequence: bootstrap throws/blocks for a project that is actually safe, breaking INIT_CHECK for correctly-configured repos like Orchestrate
preMortem.mitigation: Guard must check the ACTUAL metadata leaf path (the index.json that was added), not the .lattice prefix; verify with git check-ignore on the exact added file. Add fixtures for BOTH the broad-ignore (unsafe) and the negation-allowlist (safe, like Orchestrate .gitignore:9-18) cases asserting the guard fires only on the former.

preMortem.scenario: Doctor check misclassifies a freshly-bootstrapped safe repo as unsafe
preMortem.trigger: the new doctor invariant uses git ls-files OR check-ignore incorrectly and flags Orchestrate (which IS safe) as the data-loss state
preMortem.consequence: noise: every healthy run shows a false data-loss warning, eroding trust in doctor
preMortem.mitigation: Define the unsafe predicate precisely: metadata leaf is NOT tracked (git ls-files empty) AND NOT protected (git check-ignore shows it would be cleaned). Unit-test the predicate against three fixtures: tracked (safe), ignored-with-allowlist (safe), broad-ignore-untracked (unsafe-flagged).
